Cross-channel calibration of unknown dispersion

Source: R/dispersion_calibration.R
dispersion_calibration.Rd

Grouped multichannel models can use independent response channels to calibrate unknown noise levels before a final adaptive-ridge fit. This supplements the inexpensive ridge-pilot and bounded Pearson updates in l0glmFit().

Value

Applicable fits include dispersionCalibration, with applied, a fallback reason, or calibrated values, channel folds, calibration supports, residual degrees of freedom, timings and common-noise objective comparisons. initialDispersion and initialTheta record initialization values for the ordinary and NB drivers, respectively.

Details

control.family=list(dispersion.calibration="auto") is the default. It checks models with more selectable columns than positive-weight observations and at most ten times as many columns as observations. Calibration requires at least two grouped response channels with unknown noise parameters, automatic starts and zero ridge centers. A fourfold increase relative to the permissive initial scale, or an unsupported requested relaxed refit, triggers a residual-score check for remaining shared signal. FALSE disables calibration. TRUE bypasses the width and trigger checks, while retaining the reliability checks. Supplied positive or negative dispersions, starts and ridge centers are respected. Screening, preclustering, validation and conditional nuisance fits retain their existing estimators. Fixed-scale families require no calibration.

Channels are reproducibly split into two balanced sets, preserving the caller's RNG. A permissive, norm-based grouped pilot in one set ranks predictors for unpenalized refitting in the other set. Each calibration model retains at most 70% of its positive-weight observations in coefficient dimensions, including mandatory terms. It must retain at least eight and 20% residual degrees of freedom. The original family, link, weights, offsets and coefficient constraints are used. The family variance function gives $$\widehat\phi_c=\frac{\sum_{i:w_{ic}>0}w_{ic} (y_{ic}-\widehat\mu_{ic})^2/V(\widehat\mu_{ic})}{N_c-r_c}.$$ Here \(r_c\) is the calibration model's coefficient dimension. For Gaussian identity models with independent channel errors, selection on other channels avoids selection on the target channel's noise. If the selected span contains its mean, this is the usual unbiased residual-variance estimate. Omitted signal biases the estimate upward. For other GLMs the same argument applies to the local working model; the Pearson calculation is an approximation.

Estimated negative-binomial shape uses a bounded NB2 moment equation, $$\sum_i\frac{w_{ic}(y_{ic}-\widehat\mu_{ic})^2} {\widehat\mu_{ic}+\widehat\mu_{ic}^2/\theta_c}=\nu_c(\theta_c).$$ Unit case weights give \(\nu_c=N_c-r_c\). Unequal NB case weights use \(\nu_c=\sum_i w_{ic}(1-h_{ic})\), where \(h_{ic}\) is the diagonal of the weighted working-model projection. This accounts for the power- likelihood interpretation of NB weights. Shape bounds follow theta.min and theta.max in control.family.

Rank-deficient or inaccurate calibration fits, invalid scales and substantial residual dependence across channel sets retain the original fit. A repair requires at least a twofold reduction in estimated variance (or increase in NB shape) and an acceptable final refit. A full-response pilot supplies its start; calibrated noise parameters remain fixed during its IRLS, relaxed and local-search passes, while retaining their data-estimated parameter-count flags. Calibration refits use default iteration budgets of 60 and 100, respectively, respecting a larger supplied maxit. The repair is kept only if its penalized likelihood, or quasi-deviance kernel, improves when both models are compared at the common calibrated noise level.

Single-channel fits retain the guarded ridge initialization, bounded updates and relaxed-refit information checks. They do not sacrifice observations for a noise-calibration holdout. This fallback also applies whenever independent calibration is unavailable. l0glmTune() performs calibration within each full-data candidate and each CV training fit using only that fit's responses.

The reported likelihood and IC methods retain their conventions in model_criteria, including profiled Gaussian variance. The common-scale repair score in dispersionCalibration$objective is a separate fitting diagnostic. The channel-split adaptation implements the independent-screen/refit principle of Fan, Guo and Hao's refitted cross-validation.
